podcast.body: Released in 1992, this album was their first and led to the band being signed to Sub Pop. Sloan's emergence from Halifax contributed to the city being considered the "new Seattle" for a period, and the band went on to become a major part of the Can Rock Revolution. "Sloan, from the smeared album of 1992, they would go on to and continue to be a major part of the Can Rock Revolution."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.body: Sloan's first album, initially made with aspirations to produce 500-1000 CDs. It was later picked up and remixed by Geffen Records for a cost of $1,200, marking the band's first attempt to break into the American market on Nirvana's label. The deal eventually fell apart due to label politics, and the band was dropped. "The first record we made, which was on Geffin, we made with the aspirations of trying to make a thousand CDs or five hundred. And then we got picked up and remixed by Geffin."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 2

podcast.body: The band's first record on Geffen/DGC, initially recorded in a house in Halifax for approximately $1,200 with modest aspirations of pressing 500-1000 CDs. After signing, it was remixed by Geffen and its sound was heavily influenced by Nirvana and noisy pop bands from England like My Bloody Valentine and Ride, characterized by loud guitars. In 1996, Sloan regained the rights to this album in Canada, bringing it under their Murder Records label. "I think a lot of the records that really influenced us for smeared was, you know, the best parts of Nirvana but also the best parts of what was going on in England at the time, like my bloody Valentine and ride and all those sort of noisy pop bands that were on creation records and everything."
